summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and watery diarrhea, initially concerning for gastroenteritis. Workup revealed no infectious cause, and symptoms improved with supportive care, antiemetics, and a short course of antibiotics. He had elevated liver enzymes with AST > ALT and right upper quadrant pain; imaging showed gallstones without cholecystitis. Given his history of amiodarone use, weight loss, and elevated inflammatory markers, autoimmune hepatitis and other chronic liver conditions were considered, but a liver biopsy was deferred due to anticoagulation. His INR was supratherapeutic, prompting temporary hold of warfarin, which was restarted at discharge. He was managed for multiple comorbidities including diastolic heart failure, diabetes, and COPD. He improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in hepatology and rheumatology.
